text: Most important: the ketamine bronchodilator tile's Dosing box shows the drug store's dose (0.2-0.5 mg/kg IV, repeat q10-20 min), but the consult itself says 0.1-0.2 mg/kg IV, repeat q10-15 min, and 0.5 mg/kg/hr infusion (store: 0.5-2 mg/kg/hr). Both sit on the same tile. The reviewer replaced the tile's numeric figure with 'Sub-dissociative bolus' so the glance face does not pick either number. Not resolved here; physician to decide which dose is right.

This consult is partly a memorised sequence (adjuncts for severe asthma, BiPAP, DSI, crash airway, vent) but it also contains a severity classification, a mild-moderate pathway, PEF-based disposition and ICU orders that do not reduce to 7 actions. The strip covers the severe / life-threatening escalation only, and leaves out the first-hour basics (see the omission finding). Tiles follow the consult's node flow (nebs, Mg, ketamine, BiPAP, DSI, crash airway, vent), not the critical-actions list order. The consult forks by severity at asthma-severity but the paths are escalation levels, not different resuscitation paths, so one variant is used.

BiPAP contraindications in the consult (altered mental status unless from hypercapnia, inability to protect airway, facial trauma/burns, uncooperative patient, hemodynamic instability) are not on the tile; only 'Patient still alert and cooperative' is. Also the consult's life-threatening path (asthma-critical-decision) forks into Still conscious (BiPAP + ketamine) versus Agonal/arresting (crash airway); the strip keeps one variant, so a physician may prefer a two-variant fork there.

Time-critical content NOT on the strip: (1) severity classification, including silent chest as a dire sign (critical action on asthma-severity); (2) high-flow O2, IV steroids (methylprednisolone) and VBG/labs in the first minutes, and ipratropium with the first nebs; (3) epinephrine IM/IV for severe asthma failing SABA; (4) ketamine sedation for BiPAP tolerance (critical action on asthma-bipap-sedation) with its avoid list (propofol, high-dose benzodiazepines, opioids); (5) BiPAP contraindications beyond alert and cooperative, and inline nebulizer through the circuit; (6) DSI tube size (7.5-8.0 women, 8.0-8.5 men), the reasons for ketamine induction, and crash-airway steps before intubation (bag-mask slow breaths, intubate immediately, skip paralytic if truly agonal, largest ETT); (7) permissive hypercapnia targets (the 'do not increase rate to fix pCO2' line is quoted as the vent tile warning; the targets and the contraindications to permissive hypercapnia are not; critical action on asthma-permissive-hypercapnia); (8) vent troubleshooting (plateau >30, auto-PEEP, pneumothorax); (9) post-intubation sedation and paralysis; (10) PEF disposition thresholds (critical action on asthma-disposition-criteria) and ICU criteria. Left off to stay within 7 tiles; physician to review the choice. The reviewer notes epinephrine (IM 0.3-0.5 mg, push-dose for impending arrest) has a drug-store entry and would be a drug tile if room is made; steroids and high-flow O2 are in the consult's 'immediate simultaneous actions' list. The strip spends three of seven tiles on the intubated phase (DSI, crash airway, ventilator) and none on first-hour steroids or epinephrine: physician judgment. Tile order note: the consult's own entry points reach the crash airway (life-threatening, agonal) before DSI, but the strip keeps node-file order.

The drug store's albuterol nebulizer bronchospasm dose is 2.5 mg q20 min x 3 doses, then q1-4h PRN. It has no continuous-nebulization entry, so this is a steps tile quoting the consult's own 10-15mg/hr. The consult and the store describe different regimens for the same use; not resolved.

Crash-airway tile quotes only the already-intubated arrest steps (disconnect ETT, compress chest). The pre-intubation crash steps (bag-mask with slow breaths, ketamine 1.5-2 mg/kg, skip paralytic, largest ETT) and push-dose epinephrine are not on the strip.

Consult and store agree on 2 g IV over 20 minutes. The consult allows a repeat x1 if severe; the store says single dose. This disagreement is shown on the tile (store Dosing says single dose, 'In this consult' says can repeat x1). Not resolved.

DSI ketamine: the consult gives 1-1.5 mg/kg IV to dissociate the patient, then a separate 1-2 mg/kg IV induction dose with rocuronium 1.2 mg/kg; the store gives 1-2 mg/kg IV push once (shown as the tile figure and in Dosing). The tile now quotes the consult's four sequence lines (dissociate, BiPAP/NRB 3-5 min, induction, rocuronium) so both consult doses are visible beside the store dose; the avoid-list is the tile warning. The consult's crash-airway node gives a third ketamine dose (1.5-2 mg/kg). Not resolved.
Ketamine is dosed per kg. The store's single weight calculator for bronchodilation shows one fixed per-kg value; it does not show the consult's range or the infusion per hour.
The consult does not say how long to try BiPAP before declaring failure; it only lists tolerance routes (continue, sedate, or consider intubation).

The vent tile's figure carries a rate (8-12 breaths/min) but there is no drug-store entry for ventilator settings, so it is a steps tile. The consult gives its settings (rate, I:E, tidal volume 6-8 mL/kg IBW, PEEP, FiO2) in a table whose rows cannot be quoted line by line, so tidal volume, FiO2 and the plateau/auto-PEEP limits are not on the tile. The rate, I:E and PEEP are quoted from the node's own summary line instead.
